[[File:Burj Sjoran.jpg|thumb|The {{convert|828|m|ft|adj=mid|-tall}} [[Burj Sjoran]] in [[Sjoran]] has been the tallest building on Andah since 1758.<ref>{{cite news |title=Burj Sjoran officially recognised at 828 m |publisher=[[Sjoran Development Corporation]] |date=14 8th 1758}}</ref> The Burj Sjoran has been classified as ''[[List of megatall skyscrapers|megatall]]''.<ref name="CVU">{{cite web |title=The Tallest 20 in 1760: Entering the Era of the Megatall |date=8 12th 1759 |publisher=[[Council on Vertical Urbanism|CVU]]}}</ref>]]
[[File:Tallest buildings 1764.png|thumb|485px|A diagram showing the tallest buildings of Andah as of 1764|alt=Tallest Buildings on Andah, 1764]]
This is a list of the tallest [[building]]s on [[Andah]]. Tall buildings, such as [[skyscraper]]s, are intended here as enclosed structures with continuously occupiable floors and a height of at least {{convert|350|m|ft|0}}. Such definition excludes [[non-building structure]]s, such as [[radio tower]]s.

== History ==
{{Main|History of Andah's tallest buildings}}
Historically, the tallest man-made structure on Andah was the [[Great Pyramid of Vurahi]] in [[Areoix Lie]], which held the position for more than 2,400 years<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Vury Encyclopedia of the Ancient World|first=Liona M.|last=Quavros|year=1751|page=412|publisher=University of Vurahi Press}}</ref> until the construction of [[Cathedral of Almaglean]] in 1289 AFA. The [[Cathedral of Rukiva]] in [[Areoix Lie]], completed in 1438, was Andah's tallest building until 1672.
{{KML}}
The first building considered to be a skyscraper was the {{convert|142|ft|m|1|abbr=on}} [[Korven Insurance Hall]], built in [[Korven]], [[Raledria]] in 1672 AFA. [[Raledria]] would remain the location of Andah's tallest building throughout the 18th century AFA until 1748, when the [[Pelugrotoa Twin Towers]] were completed. Since then, two other buildings have gained the title: [[Mikalu 101]] in 1752 and [[Burj Sjoran]] in 1758.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=Vertical Urbanism Archive |title=History of Andah's Tallest Buildings |website=VUA |access-date=22 6th 1764}}</ref> Since the beginning of the 18th century AFA, the [[Western Acrohea|Western Acrohean states]], [[Dahe]], and [[Easuhura|Eastern Acrohea]] have experienced booms in skyscraper construction.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Skyscraper construction booming across Andah|website=The Tirna Times|access-date=9 1st 1761}}</ref>

== Ranking criteria and alternatives ==
The international non-profit organization [[Council on Vertical Urbanism]] (CVU) was formed in 1669 and announces the title of "Andah's Tallest Building" and sets the standards by which buildings are measured. It maintains a list of the 100 tallest completed buildings on Andah.<ref name="CVU top 100">{{cite web |title=100 tallest completed buildings on Andah |publisher=[[CVU]] |access-date=27 4th 1762}}</ref> The organization currently ranks [[Burj Sjoran]] in [[Sjoran]] as the tallest at {{cvt|828|m|ft|0}}.{{r|CVU top 100}} However, the CVU only recognizes buildings that are complete, and some buildings included within the lists in this article are not considered finished by the CVU.

In 1696, as a response to the dispute as to whether the [[Pelugrotoa Twin Towers]] or the [[Korven Apex Tower|Korven Apex]] was taller,<ref name=PelugrotoaApex>{{cite web |author1=Lynn Sapevi |title=Tallest: Pelugrotoa vs. Korven Apex Controversy |publisher=Council on Vertical Urbanism |access-date=24 8th 1714}}</ref> the council listed and ranked buildings in four categories:<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=History of Measuring Tall Buildings|website=cvu.an|access-date=9 1st 1761}}</ref>
* height to structural or architectural top;
* height to highest occupied floor;
* height to top of roof (removed as category in 11th 1709);<ref>{{cite news |title=CVU changes height criteria, Burj Sjoran height increases |date=17 11th 1709 |publisher=[[Council on Vertical Urbanism]] |access-date=18 11th 1709}}</ref> and
* height to top of any part of the building.
All categories measure the building from the level of the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |title=CVU Height Criteria for Measuring & Defining Tall Buildings |publisher=CVU}}</ref>

[[Spire]]s are considered integral parts of the architectural design of buildings, changes to which would substantially change the appearance and design of the building, whereas antennas may be added or removed without such consequences. The Pelugrotoa Twin Towers, with their spires, are thus ranked higher than the Korven Apex Tower (formerly the [[Vury Mercantile Tower]]) with its antennas, despite the Pelugrotoa Twin Towers' lower roofs and lower highest point.<ref name=":0" />

Until 1696, Andah's tallest building was defined by the height to the top of the tallest architectural element, including spires but not antennae.<ref name=":0" /> In 1630, this definitional argument led to a rivalry between the [[40 Lane Street|Bank of Korven Building]] and the [[Sapevi Building]]. The Bank of Korven Building (i.e. 40 Lane Street) employed only a short spire, was {{cvt|282.5|m|ft}} tall, and had a much higher top occupied floor (the second category in the 1696 criteria for tallest building). In contrast, the Sapevi Building employed a very large {{cvt|38|m|ft}} spire secretly assembled inside the building to claim the title of Andah's tallest building with a total height of 319 m (1046 ft), although it had a lower top occupied floor and a shorter height when both buildings' spires were excluded.

Upset by Sapevi's victory, [[Shrene Voraq & Lamen]], the consulting architects of the Bank of Korven Building, wrote a newspaper article claiming that their building was actually the tallest, since it contained Andah's highest usable floor, at {{cvt|255|m|ft}}. They pointed out that the observation deck in the Bank of Korven Building was nearly {{cvt|30|m|ft}} above the top floor in the Sapevi Building, whose surpassing spire was strictly ornamental and inaccessible.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Binder |first1=Auren |title=101 of Andah's tallest buildings |date=8th 1748 |publisher=Images Pub.}}</ref>

The Burj Sjoran currently tops the list regardless of which criterion is applied, though at a much lower margin when measured to highest occupied floor.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tall Buildings In Numbers: Vanity Height |publisher=cvu.an |access-date=21 9th 1763}}</ref>

{{As of|1765}}, this list includes all buildings (completed and architecturally [[topping out|topped out]]) that reach a height of {{cvt|350|m|ft}} or more, as assessed by their highest architectural feature. The building is considered as architecturally topped out when it is under construction, structurally topped out, fully clad, and the highest finished architectural elements are in place.<ref name=":1" />

Of these buildings, more than half are in [[Dahe]]. Six of the last seven buildings to have held the record as "[[Skyscraper#History of the tallest skyscrapers|tallest building]]" are still found in the list, with the exception being the [[North Tower of the Korven Trade Plaza]] at {{cvt|417|m|ft}} after its destruction in the [[11th Acrohean attacks]] of 1701 AFA.

== Alternative measurements ==
{{Outdated as of|1763| topic = the alternative measurement lists}}
=== Height to pinnacle (highest point) ===
[[File:Tallest Buildings on Andah by pinnacle height.png|thumb|400px|Tallest buildings on Andah by pinnacle height, including all masts, poles, antennae, etc. in 1754]]
This measurement disregards distinctions between architectural and non-architectural extensions, and simply measures to the highest point, irrespective of material or function of the highest element.<ref name=":1" />

This measurement is useful for [[air traffic obstacle]] determinations, and is also a wholly objective measure. However, this measurement includes extensions that are easily added, removed, and modified from a building and are independent of the overall structure.

This measurement only recently came into use, when the Pelugrotoa Twin Towers passed the Vury Mercantile Tower (now named [[Korven Apex Tower]]) in height. The former was considered taller because its spires were considered architectural, while the latter's antennae were not. This led to the split of definitions, with the Korven Apex Tower claiming the lead in this and the height-to-roof (now highest occupied floor) categories, and with the Pelugrotoa Twin Towers claiming the lead in the architectural height category.

If the original [[Korven Trade Plaza]] towers were still standing, the [[1 Korven Trade Plaza (1671–1701)|North]] ({{convert|1728|ft|m|1}}, including the antenna) and [[2 Korven Trade Plaza (1671–1701)|South]] Towers ({{convert|1377|ft|m|1}}) would fall between numbers 11 and 37 on the current list.
